# FRICTION_INDEX.md — every logged friction item, rolled up by surface

**Generated. Do not edit by hand.**
`python3 tools/friction_index.py` rewrites this file from
`campaign/friction/*.md`; `python3 tools/friction_index.py --check` fails when
it has drifted, and `tools/audit_docs.py` runs that check as its `friction`
class, so an index that no longer matches the logs is a doc-audit finding.

The friction logs are the repo's record of what fights back when a model
drives this engine. Read as prose they are 20+ separate complaints; read as
this table they are a work queue ordered by blast radius. A surface that
several independent campaigns hit is not bad luck — it is a specification for
a fix.

## What this counts, and what it cannot see

- **One row per `surface` token.** The rollup key is the `surface:` field the
  friction contract requires on every item. Tokens are compared lowercased
  with backticks stripped and whitespace collapsed — nothing smarter. Two
  spellings of the same surface are two rows, and that is the failure mode to
  watch for: run `--surfaces` before inventing a token.
- **"logs" counts DISTINCT source files, not items.** Three items in one
  campaign's file are one log. The campaign column excludes the two
  cross-campaign logs (`ENGINE.md`, `_digest_phase_findings.md`), which are
  not campaigns; they still count as a log and still appear in the
  occurrences.
- **Worst severity is the worst grade any occurrence carries**, and a fixed
  item keeps the grade it earned — severity records what it cost, `status`
  records whether it still costs it.
- **`note` items are excluded from every row.** They are context the authors
  kept on purpose ("what worked better than expected"), not friction.
- **It cannot see friction nobody logged.** Every campaign that solved a
  problem silently is invisible here, and the corpus is retrospective: items
  were graded in one pass against the evidence in each entry, so a grade is
  an honest reading of the write-up, not a re-run of the failure.
- **It cannot tell you a row is one BUG.** It tells you several campaigns
  named one surface. Whether those are one defect or four unrelated ones in
  the same file is a judgement the reader makes from the linked entries — the
  index points, it does not diagnose.
- **`status` is what the logs say.** An item is `fixed` here because an entry,
  a `RESOLUTIONS` section or a `Fix log` in the same file says so. This tool
  does not re-verify a fix against the binary.

## Using it

```sh
python3 tools/friction_index.py --surfaces          # every token in use
python3 tools/friction_index.py --surface union_all # every item on one surface
python3 tools/friction_index.py --json              # the rollup, machine-readable
python3 tools/friction_index.py --check             # is this file stale?
```

Before a campaign logs a new item it checks this table for the surface it is
about to name; when it finds one, its own entry carries a `recurrence of:`
line and the final self-check lists the id (DELIVERABLE_SPEC, "Recurrence
stated"). That is what keeps a defect from being rediscovered in silence.
